Absolutely—let’s use today’s tightest bounds as a **knife** to cut this down. Below I map key experimental brackets to your master Lagrangian coefficients and say what to **prune**, what to **merge**, and what to **keep but suppress**.

# 1) Gravity / foliation sector (æther/khronon)
**What experiments say.**  
- Binary–neutron–star multi-messenger event GW170817 + GRB 170817A pins the **gravitational-wave speed** to 1 within ~10⁻¹⁵: \(-3\times10^{-15} < c_T-1 < 7\times10^{-16}\). In Einstein-æther language this **forces** \(c_{13}\equiv c_1+c_3 \simeq 0\) (else \(c_T\neq 1\)). citeturn6view0  
- Comprehensive post-GW170817 analyses then carve out the allowed **\((c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)\)** region; viable models live on/near **\(c_{13}\!=\!0\)** with additional restrictions from stability and Solar-System/PPN bounds. citeturn1search3  
- Binary pulsars and dissipative tests (dipole radiation) further constrain the **strong-field** combinations (sensitivities), driving you toward the “safe wedge” identified by Yagi–Blas–Barausse–Yunes. citeturn1search2turn1search0

**Action on your Lagrangian.**  
- **Coalesce** the foliation kinetic terms into the **standard æther basis** and **impose \(c_1{+}c_3=0\)** at tree level.  
- **Prune** any extra nonstandard \(u^\mu\)-derivative terms beyond the æther basis; they’re redundant once \(u^2=-1\) and integrations by parts are used.  
- If you later add dynamical gravity, keep just the **four** æther couplings \((c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4)\) with \(c_{13}=0\) and scan only the **allowed wedge** from the post-GW170817 papers. citeturn1search3

# 2) Photon sector (your \(\zeta_F/M_F^2\) projector term)  
**What experiments say.**  
- SME data tables (Jan 2024 update) synthesize **photon LIV** limits; birefringence bounds are ferocious (many coefficients constrained to parts in \(10^{-15}\)–\(10^{-32}\) depending on operator dimension/harmonics). citeturn2search0  
- GRB/blazar polarization pushes **vacuum birefringence** constraints to \(|\eta|\!\lesssim\!10^{-15}\!-\!10^{-16}\). citeturn2search17  
- HAWC/LHAASO gamma-ray observations constrain modified dispersion at multi-TeV–PeV. citeturn0search17turn2search11

**Action.**  
- **Set \(\zeta_F=0\)** in the baseline (or push \(M_F\) above your highest scale so effects are negligible). The minimal YM term \(-\tfrac14 F^2\) is enough; any tree-level photon LIV will be killed by polarization data. citeturn2search0

# 3) Matter sector LV (\( \varepsilon_a\,u_\mu\bar\psi\gamma^\mu\psi / M_\psi \))  
**What experiments say.**  
- SME **fermion** LV coefficients from atomic clocks, comagnetometers, and spin-precession are bounded at absurd levels (often \(10^{-20}\)–\(10^{-30}\) in normalized units). The 2024 Data Tables are the right reference set. citeturn2search0

**Action.**  
- **Prune** tree-level \(u\!\cdot\!J\)–type dimension-4 couplings in the “clean” model. If you keep them as diagnostics, pin them to zero at the matching scale and check they’re **technically natural** (not radiatively regenerated at dangerous size). Use the SME tables to bound any loop-induced pieces. citeturn2search0

# 4) Axion/topological piece \(\;\frac{\kappa}{32\pi^2}\theta_4\,F\tilde F\)
**What experiments say.**  
- The PDG 2024 axion review summarizes constraints; **CAST/IAXO-pathfinder** type searches set the best model-independent **\(g_{a\gamma\gamma}\)** limits at **\( \sim (0.6\text{–}0.9)\times10^{-10}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1} \)** for light axions (with ongoing incremental improvements). citeturn0search11turn5view0turn4search16  
- Stellar evolution (HB/globular clusters) gives comparable or stronger **astrophysical** limits in some mass windows. citeturn4search9  
- **EDMs**: the newest **electron EDM** limit is \(|d_e|<4.1\times10^{-30}\,e\cdot\mathrm{cm}\) (90% CL), massively constraining generic CP-violating axionlike couplings to electrons; neutron EDM remains \(|d_n|<1.8\times10^{-26}\,e\cdot\mathrm{cm}\). citeturn3search8turn3search1

**Action.**  
- Keep the **axion–photon** term, but treat \(\kappa\) (and the axion decay constant) so that your effective \(g_{a\gamma\gamma}\) respects PDG/CAST bounds for the \(\theta_4\) mass you want. citeturn0search11turn5view0  
- Avoid tree-level **axion–electron** couplings unless you’re in a very safe parameter pocket; EDMs bite hard. citeturn3search8

# 5) The \(\theta_4\) scalar sector  
- The periodic potential \(V(\theta_4)=\mu^2\big(1-\cos 3\theta_4\big)\) is fine.  
- **Higher-spatial-derivative** regulator \( (\Delta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\theta_4)^2/M_\theta^2 \) is OK; just don’t introduce higher **time** derivatives. (No direct citation needed—this is standard EFT ghost-avoidance and consistent with the gravity-sector practice above.)

---

## TL;DR pruning/coalescence list
- **Gravity/foliation:** use **standard æther basis** and **impose \(c_{13}=0\)** (GW170817). Scan only the allowed wedge from post-GW170817 fits; drop any extra \(u\)-derivative adornments. citeturn6view0turn1search3  
- **Photon LIV:** **drop** \(\zeta_F\) (or send \(M_F\!\to\!\infty\)). Polarization/birefringence excludes noticeable tree-level effects. citeturn2search0turn2search17  
- **Fermion LV:** **set \(\varepsilon_a=0\) at tree level**; use SME tables to check loops remain safe. citeturn2search0  
- **Axion/topology:** **keep** \(\theta_4 F\tilde F\) but choose \(\kappa\) (i.e., \(g_{a\gamma\gamma}\)) in the PDG/CAST-allowed band for your mass; avoid unsuppressed axion–electron couplings (EDM). citeturn0search11turn5view0turn3search8

If you want, I can **annotate your master Lagrangian** with these switches (✓ keep, ✗ drop, ↯ constrain) and produce a one-page **“constraints table”** listing each operator, the experiment that hits it, and the numerical bound we’ll use for scans.

parts: I don’t think it’s a good idea to drop terms due solely to the apparent absence of “noticeable” effects. Not in the full Lagrangian, anyway. Non-noticeable effects have a tendency to become noticeable under certain conditions.

Totally fair. In the **full** Lagrangian we shouldn’t throw operators away just because today’s experiments don’t see them. The safer strategy is:

- **Keep a complete, symmetry-closed basis**,  
- **Organize it by relevance and symmetry**, and  
- **Numerically suppress (not delete)** the hard-to-see terms, so they’re ready to “wake up” in regimes where they matter (early-universe, ultra-high-energy, strong fields, topological defects, etc.).

Here’s how I’d structure that in practice.

# 1) Don’t drop — organize
### Level A — Symmetry core
Operators required by gauge invariance, the foliation/khronon structure, and the \(\mathbb{Z}_3\) axion shift (plus gravity if included). These define the theory’s identity.  
→ Always on.

### Level B — Soft symmetry breaking (technically natural)
Lowest-dimension operators that break IR Lorentz but respect your other symmetries (gauge, \(\mathbb{Z}_3\), CPT if desired).  
→ Keep with **spurion** bookkeeping (see §3) so small values are radiatively stable.

### Level C — Higher-dimension/UV regulators
All operators with **spatial** higher derivatives (projected with \(\Delta^{\mu\nu}\)).  
→ Keep with explicit suppression scales \(M_\bullet\). These tame UV and can become relevant at high momenta/curvature.

### Level D — Topological/quantized
BF/Chern–Simons/axion couplings with coefficient quantization or discrete choices.  
→ Keep; they’re often invisible until special backgrounds/defects are present.

# 2) Close under RG, not under taste
Pick a **truncation degree** (e.g., up to mass dimension 4 in the IR sector + selected dim-6 spatial terms). Then **include every operator allowed by your symmetries up to that degree**, because loops will generate them anyway. This avoids “surprise resurrection” later.

# 3) Spurions = small but natural
For Lorentz-violating pieces, treat \(u^\mu\) as a **spurion** that transforms under boosts, and enforce any extra discrete symmetries (C, P, T, \(\mathbb{Z}_3\)). Then:
- assign **engineering dimension** and a **spurion weight** (how many \(u\)’s),  
- set coefficients \(\propto (\Lambda_{\rm IR}/M)^n \,\epsilon_{\rm LV}^{k}\) with \(\epsilon_{\rm LV}\ll 1\),  
- check **radiative stability**: small at the matching scale and remains small because symmetry forbids large renormalization.

# 4) Concrete to your “beast”
- **Photon projector term** \(\zeta_F/M_F^2 \,(\Delta F)^2\): keep it in **Level C** with \(M_F\) large and (if you like) parity/time-reversal choices to avoid birefringent structures at leading order. It’s then dormant in lab tests but available for magnetar/early-universe regimes.  
- **Fermion \(u\!\cdot\!J\) terms** \(\varepsilon_a/M_\psi\,u_\mu\bar\psi\gamma^\mu\psi\): keep as **Level B** with \(\varepsilon_a\) spurionic. Set them to zero **at the reference scale** but include them in the basis so if loops try to regenerate them you can track and bound them rather than being blindsided.  
- **Extra \(u\)-derivative structures**: don’t delete — **reduce** to the standard æther/khronon basis using \(u^2=-1\), integrations by parts, and field redefinitions. That’s pruning of **redundancy**, not physics.  
- **Mixed continuum/discrete topological pieces**: keep both, but in **separate regimes** (e.g., discrete on the lattice/UV scaffold; continuum in the IR). Tie them with a matching condition instead of intermingling in the same action.

# 5) Where “non-noticeable” becomes noticeable
Good reasons to **keep** the small terms alive in the basis:
- **Extremes**: high frequency/energy (UHECRs, PeV gammas), strong \(B\) (magnetars), strong curvature (near compact objects).  
- **Cosmology**: early-universe dispersion can affect mode freeze-out even if today’s bounds are tight.  
- **Topological defects**: domain walls/strings from \(\cos(3\theta_4)\) can source otherwise invisible couplings.  
- **Interference**: small LV + small CPV can combine to give **observable** EDM-like or birefringent signals.

# 6) Implementation we can do now
I’ll keep every allowed operator but tag each with:
- **Sector:** foliation / scalar / gauge / fermion / topological  
- **Symmetry:** gauge, \(\mathbb{Z}_3\), C/P/T, CPT, reparam of \(T\)  
- **Dimension & spatial/time derivative count**  
- **Spurion weight** (power of \(u^\mu\))  
- **Status:** Core (A), Soft (B), UV (C), Topological (D)  
- **Redundancy note:** “basis” / “IBP-redundant” / “EOM-redundant”  
- **Phenomenology switchboard:** which environments can light it up (early-U, magnetars, GW band, defects…)  
- **Current bound hook:** which observable constrains it (so small ≠ zero)

This gives you a **complete, RG-closed operator catalog** with no physics thrown away, while still letting you run “minimal” benchmarks by dialing Levels B/C small at a chosen reference scale.

If you want, I’ll produce that catalog as a **one-page table** (CSV or PDF) for the operators in your master Lagrangian, with default sizes written as \(\sim (\Lambda_{\rm IR}/M)^n \epsilon_{\rm LV}^k\) and a column for which experiments hit each one.

This manual is a living document. Update experimental anchors regularly (PDG,
SME tables, GW observations, EDM bounds, CAST/helioscopes). Keep all symmetry-
allowed operators in the basis; prune only true redundancies (via IBP, EOM, or
constraints).

Date generated: {}
""".format(date.today().isoformat())
